title: [app-shell] ActionParamDialog `filterVisibleParams` resolves a broken param `visible` SILENTLY, and in a direction decided by the predicate's dialect
body:
Found while verifying objectstack-ai/objectstack#8500. Filed unassigned for triage — it is a
**different evaluation face** from that card (action *param* visibility, not action
visibility), and either way of fixing it flips a deliberately-pinned test, so it wants its
own decision rather than a rider.

## Where

`packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.tsx`, `filterVisibleParams` — the gate in
front of every param the action param-collection dialog offers:

```ts
return params.filter((p) => {
  if (!p.visible) return true;
  try {
    return evaluator.evaluateCondition(p.visible);
  } catch {
    return true;
  }
});
```

This is also, almost certainly, the site objectstack#8500 quoted out of the minified
`RecordDetailView-*.js` chunk as `try { return n.evaluateCondition(e.visible) } catch { return true }`
— `.visible` read off a loop variable matches here literally, and the dialog is in that
chunk. (The header-action path that card is *about* is a different one and behaves
correctly; see the report on that card.)

## Measured

Probed directly against `filterVisibleParams` on `main` (`5bf5d2cb6`), scope
`{ os: { user: { id: 'u1' } }, record: { manager: 'u1' } }`, one param:

| `visible` | param kept? | warnings |
|---|---|---|
| `record.@@@ bad` (unparseable) | **kept (fail-open)** | **0 — silent** |
| `nope_undeclared == 1` (undeclared identifier) | **kept (fail-open)** | **0 — silent** |
| `${record.missing.id == 1}` (legacy dialect, faults) | **dropped (fail-closed)** | **0 — silent** |
| `{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'not ] valid (' }` | kept (fail-open) | 1 |
| `{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'os.user.id == record.manager.id' }` | kept (fail-open) | 1 |
| `os.user.id == "u1"` / `== "u2"` | kept / dropped | 0 (genuine verdicts) |

Two things fall out:

1. **Silence.** Three of the fault rows emit nothing at all. That is the state the standing
   2026-08-06 ruling on #4051 / objectstack#5149 names as the one option that is not
   available: fail-open or fail-closed may be chosen, **silent may not**. Only the
   `{ dialect, source }` envelope rows are loud, and they are loud by accident — the
   canonical helper one layer down warns for them, not this function.
2. **The fail direction is decided by the predicate's dialect, not by the surface.** A bare
   string routes to the legacy JS evaluator (lenient, returns falsy, param silently
   DROPPED); an envelope routes to CEL (faults, param silently KEPT). One `visible` key,
   two opposite outcomes, chosen by whether the authored text happens to contain `${…}` /
   `===` — which is the objectui#3314 shape, on a function that never got the
   `toPredicateInput` / `evalRowPredicate` conversion the rest of the predicate faces did.

Impact is asymmetric and both halves are bad: a silently DROPPED param means the dialog
never collects a value the server requires, so the action fails on submit with nothing
pointing at the predicate; a silently KEPT one offers a field the backend rejects, which is
the exact case `create_user`'s `features.phoneNumber == true` gate exists to prevent.

## Why this needs a decision rather than a patch

Neither obvious fix is verdict-neutral, and each flips a test that was pinned on purpose in
`ActionParamDialog.test.tsx`:

- **`throwOnError: true` + fail-open + warn** flips *"hides a feature-gated param when the
  flag is absent (conservative)"* — under CEL a missing key is a fault, so
  `features.phoneNumber == true` against `features: {}` would start SHOWING the param.
- **`throwOnError: true` + fail-closed + warn** keeps that one but flips *"defaults to
  visible when the predicate is malformed (fail-open)"*, and fail-closed on a param can
  hide a field the user must fill.
- **Routing through the canonical `evalRowPredicate`** (which is what would end the dialect
  split and get the warn-once + label for free) additionally re-pins `record` / `data` to
  the row, and this surface's scope is the host predicate scope, which carries its own
  `data`. That shadowing is a behaviour change on its own.

My recommendation, for what it is worth: **fail-open + loud**, on the canonical entry, with
the `data` shadowing handled explicitly — a hidden required param is the harder failure to
diagnose than an extra field the server rejects with a message. But the conservative
feature-flag case is a real requirement pulling the other way and should be ruled on, not
guessed.

Blocked-by: nothing. Related: #4051 (the funnel that was loudened in rc.5),
objectstack-ai/objectstack#8500 (where this was measured), #3314 (one value, one answer).
